question: each hand3 finger moves round the hub ring independently

C.patterns: one finger alone, two neighbours, all four; not two opposite, not three (plane: z0 + z2 = z1 + z3)

G.note: sensored FOC controller rated 55 A phase + shaft encoder replaces the planned ESC (est.)

H.shaft: SE 2816 shaft is solid: no bore for wires

table.name: Keep hub E (two rings, mirror spread)
table.What each finger can do: All four together. Neighbours swing opposite ways into two pairs, 0-47°. Roots fixed at 45/135/225/315°.
table.Actuators (rotating or not): 2 x STS3215, not rotating (base ring: spread + K1; curl ring: K2 + K3).
table.What crosses to the spinning side: Nothing. Yoke lips hook the ring flange across a 1 mm gap.
table.Balance in flight: Self-centring: centrifugal pull returns each finger to the cross with 7.7 N m at 47° (lag spring 5.4 mN m).
table.Centrifugal load at 12,500 rpm: No new parts. Each finger pulls 826 N on its lag pin (3,493 x gravity at r 20).
table.Force / torque: have vs need: Base cord 104 N stall / 35 N rated per finger; need 55 / 22 N: margin 1.89 / 1.58. Stall 65 W at 12 V.
table.Hub \u00d8 / height: Ø81.6, no change. Stack margin 1.1 mm.
table.Main risk: Does not do what was asked.

table.name: Third nested ring (pairs split)
table.What each finger can do: Each PAIR on its own (F1+F4, F2+F3); inside a pair still mirrored. Works at any rotor angle.
table.Added mass: +3.7 g rotating ring; hand about 471 g (+75, est.).
table.Balance in flight: Self-centring as A. Ring is closed and round: balanced.
table.Centrifugal load at 12,500 rpm: Closed ring: hoop load only, no net force.
table.Force / torque: have vs need: One servo per two fingers: 207 N stall per finger, margin 3.78. Stall 97 W.
table.Parts to buy: 1 x STS3215, 2 x Ø3 carbon rod, 2 x MR63 bearing.
table.Hub \u00d8 / height: Ø86.6 (+5); hand +16.7 mm long (one more flange level). Four rings: Ø97, +50 mm: rejected.
table.Main risk: Longer wrist lever for a half answer; a ring per finger does not fit.

table.name: Tilting base ring (3 pull points)
table.What each finger can do: One finger alone, two neighbours, or all four. Not two opposite, not three (cord anchors stay in one plane).
table.Actuators (rotating or not): 4 x STS3215, not rotating (3 on the base ring, 1 curl).
table.Added mass: about 0 g rotating; hand about 514 g (+118, est.).
table.Balance in flight: Self-centring as A; ring must sit flat before spin-up (3 servo positions).
table.Centrifugal load at 12,500 rpm: No new rotor parts; a tilted ring would wobble, so flat is a spin-up condition.
table.Force / torque: have vs need: Tilt 19° needs 3.9 mm bore clearance, ring has 0.8: new ball-type guide. Rim rises 3.6 mm, 1.0 mm left under the roots. Stall 130 W.
table.Parts to buy: 2 x STS3215, 2 x Ø3 rod, MR63 bearings.
table.Hub \u00d8 / height: Ø unchanged; servo block one servo wider or taller (est.).
table.Main risk: Ring jams or keys bind when tilted; only some patterns.

table.name: Base ring cut into four sectors, 4 pullers
table.What each finger can do: EACH finger on its own: any spread 0-47°, then its own K1 fold. Curl (K2 + K3) stays shared. Roots stay at the cross.
table.Actuators (rotating or not): 4 x STS3032 (20 g) + 1 x STS3215, all not rotating. The four small servos fill today's upper servo bay.
table.What crosses to the spinning side: Nothing. Four lips hook four flange sectors; rotor parks within ±24°.
table.Added mass: +1.5 g rotating (keys); hand about 454 g (+58, est.).
table.Balance in flight: Self-centring as A: by 1,046 rpm the centrifugal return is 10 x the lag spring. Rule: all pullers released before spin-up.
table.Centrifugal load at 12,500 rpm: Each sector 1.2 g at r 27: 57 N on its key (7 MPa on 8 mm², PA-CF). Four equal sectors: balanced.
table.Force / torque: have vs need: STS3032 on Ø6 spool: 83 N stall / 28 N rated; margin 1.51 / 1.26 (target 1.25 / 1.0). Stall 61 W; 6 V rail 4.8 A.
table.Parts to buy: 4 x Feetech STS3032, 4 x Ø3 carbon rod, 8 x MR63, 6 V 5 A buck regulator (est.).
table.Hub \u00d8 / height: Ø81.6 and height unchanged (est.). Servo bay 46.4 vs 45.2 mm: +1.2 mm. Rod pairs 9.4 mm apart.
table.Main risk: A sector cocks on its key under an off-centre pull; sideways pinch is weak (0.9 N).

table.name: One ring + pick-up latch per finger
table.What each finger can do: Each finger is IN or OUT of the base stroke. Those that are in move together by the same amount.
table.Actuators (rotating or not): 2 x STS3215 + 1 x SCS0009 selector (13 g), not rotating.
table.What crosses to the spinning side: Nothing; the selector flips latches only when parked within ±1.4°.
table.Added mass: +3.6 g rotating; hand about 421 g (+25, est.).
table.Balance in flight: Self-centring as A. A latch that flips in flight does nothing (cords are slack).
table.Centrifugal load at 12,500 rpm: Each 0.4 g latch at r 20: 14 N, taken by the cage slot; it must slide along the axis so the load cannot flip it.
table.Force / torque: have vs need: One finger alone gets the whole ring: 415 N stall (TPU link limits it). Stall 71 W.
table.Parts to buy: 1 x Feetech SCS0009; 4 printed latches, Ø1.5 pins.
table.Main risk: ±1° parking again (rev D's weak point); small latches at 3,500 x gravity; no in-between angles.

table.name: Roots on carrier rings, roller + pawl index
table.What each finger can do: Each ROOT travels round the hub in 15° steps: 3 + 1 thumb, 2 + 2, all four inside 135°. Roots no closer than 45°. Spread and curl as A.
table.Actuators (rotating or not): 2 x STS3215 + STS3032 roller drive + SCS0009 cam (roller in, pawl in). Not rotating.
table.What crosses to the spinning side: Nothing. Roller and pawl touch the rotor only when parked.
table.Added mass: +12 g rotating (est.); hand about 452 g (+55, est.).
table.Balance in flight: NOT self-centring. Must be back at the cross and locked before spin-up: 1° off = 14 N, one step off = 216 N, 3 + 1 = 1168 N. V-seats at 0.05 mm: 1.9 N (today's pins: 2.1 N).
table.Centrifugal load at 12,500 rpm: Each carrier takes its finger's 826 N (1093 N proof). 1.5 mm 6061 leaves: 55 MPa tension, 55 MPa bearing (yield 276). Lag tube bending 222 MPa: too high, needs a stiffer pin.
table.Force / torque: have vs need: Roller needs 11 mN m, has 147: x14. 90° in 0.4 s. Dogs carry 14 N. Stall 78 W.
table.Parts to buy: STS3032, SCS0009, laser-cut 6061 leaves (8), Ø14 spindle, 4 dog pins + springs, Hall sensor + 4 magnets.
table.Hub \u00d8 / height: Hub stack 12 mm (today 10); Ø unchanged (est.). New hub, cage and cord followers.
table.Main risk: A missed lock is a destroyed hand; whole rotor hub redesigned and re-proofed.

table.name: Carrier rings, flight motor indexes vs pawl
table.Actuators (rotating or not): 2 x STS3215 + SCS0009 pawl. The SE 2816 itself turns the hub to each new angle.
table.Balance in flight: As F: locked cross is a hard spin-up condition.
table.Force / torque: have vs need: Motor has 0.62 N m, indexing needs about 0.03: plenty. But the planned ESC cannot hold an angle at zero speed.
table.Parts to buy: Sensored FOC drive for 54 A + shaft encoder in place of the ESC (est.), SCS0009, carrier parts as F.
table.Main risk: Changes the motor drive of a flight-critical rotor for a parked-only feature.

table.name: Servos on the rotor, slip ring
table.What crosses to the spinning side: Slip ring for power + data: 6 wires, 2 A, rated 300 rpm (Adafruit 736). Rotor runs 12,500 rpm: 42 x over.
table.Balance in flight: Every 1 g out of place at r 20 is 34 N of shake.
table.Centrifugal load at 12,500 rpm: A 9 g servo at r 20 weighs 308 N (31 kgf).
table.Force / torque: have vs need: Not sized: fails before torque matters.
table.Main risk: Already rejected in the hub rethink (option E there); the motor shaft is solid.
